subject: Evidence request: data localization and erasure controls for SOC2/ISO
messages:
From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@meditech.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@meditech.com>, ISO Audit Team <iso@meditech.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2/ISO evidence: data residency, retention & deletion questions

Hannah —

Following up from our audit kick-off: our SOC2 Type II auditor and internal ISO reviewer have a focused set of questions around data residency, retention, and proof-of-deletion for user data (customer request and platform logs). Can you confirm the following and share evidence where possible?

1) Data residency options: confirmation of region(s) where customer request/metadata and derived outputs can be stored for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments.
2) Retention windows and configurable defaults for request logs, model prompts, embeddings, and backups (what's default, and how to request shorter windows).
3) Deletion mechanics: what constitutes proof-of-deletion (object manifest, deletion marker, snapshots removed, backup retention behavior).
4) Evidence artifacts auditors typically accept (policy docs, runbooks, deletion manifests, immutable audit logs, timestamped API call logs).
5) For EU customers: ability to demonstrate deletion within EU region and assurance that backups are erased / rotated in line with deletion request.

Deadline: auditor asked for initial evidence by 2026-04-06 to keep us on schedule. Please flag anything you cannot provide by that date.

Thanks — we appreciate concise artifacts (one-pagers + a short index).

Regards,
Alice Jensen
Sr. IT Compliance Manager
MediTech Solutions
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@meditech.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2/ISO evidence: data residency, retention & deletion questions

Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble a concise evidence pack and an ownerable action plan. High-level answers below; I attached a retention matrix and an evidence index (see attachments) — engineering and compliance will produce the artifacts you can share with your auditor.

Answers (summary):
- Data residency: Hosted: US (us-west/us-east) and EU regions available per customer selection; Dedicated: deployed to customer-chosen region/Cloud account; Private: customer-managed VPC/on-prem. We'll include the region mapping in the evidence index.
- Retention defaults: request logs (90 days default, configurable down to 7 days for hosted), prompts and generated outputs (90 days default; customers may opt-in to short-lived storage in Dedicated/Private), embedding vectors (by default retained 365 days for feature indexing; configurable), backups/snapshots (30–90 day retention depending on tier; longer retention for backups is opt-in and captured in the matrix).
- Deletion mechanics & proof: we provide deletion manifests (object keys + deletion timestamp + API request id), immutable audit logs (WORM-styled append logs containing admin API calls), and backend GC run logs showing successful removal. For hosted customers we can provide proof-of-deletion artifacts consisting of: deletion_manifest_<account>_<date>.txt, audit_log_slice_<date>.ndjson, and snapshot_gc_report_<date>.pdf.
- Backups and replication: backups are stored following configured region policy; for EU residency we retain backups in-region unless customer chooses cross-region replication. We will supply a backup-erasure playbook that shows the steps and timestamps when backups are tombstoned and eligible for physical purge.
- Evidence auditors accept: policy doc (retention-policy-v2), runbook (deletion-runbook-v2), deletion manifests, audit log extracts, and a mapping spreadsheet tying policies to control IDs (we've attached an initial index).

I'll coordinate with Marcus (engineering lead) and Neha (security/compliance) to generate the technical artifacts you requested. We'll aim to deliver the attachments by 2026-04-02 to give your auditor time to review before your deadline. If any of the items are restricted for hosted tenants due to multi-tenant architecture, we'll call that out explicitly and offer alternative artifacts (e.g., aggregated proof + per-account deletion manifests).

Next step: can we set a 30-minute call on Tues 2026-03-30 to confirm exactly which evidence items your auditor will accept?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2/ISO evidence: data residency, retention & deletion questions

Hannah —

Couple of operational notes for the artifacts we'll produce:
1) For customer-specific deletion proofs we'll export the object manifest produced by the server-side delete job, include the GC job id, and attach the storage provider's delete-confirmation where available. Example filename: proof_of_deletion_meditech_requests_20260328.txt.
2) We need to preserve an immutable audit slice (ndjson) with admin API calls that reference the deletion request id. That slice will be pulled from the audit-store and time-bound to the deletion window requested by the auditor.
3) For Hosted customers where we can't release internal storage-level metadata, we'll provide per-account API call traces + hashed object ids in the manifest and a signed statement of GC completion from the SRE lead.
4) EU residency: ensure the snapshot_gc_report explicitly lists the snapshot storage location and the KMS key id used to encrypt it. The auditor will want to see that the KMS key is also region-bound (or customer-managed in Dedicated/Private).

Will produce: deletion_manifest, audit_log_slice, snapshot_gc_report, and a short runbook excerpt that maps each artifact to the control it satisfies (e.g., CC6.1 — data disposal).

Marcus
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@meditech.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2/ISO evidence: data residency, retention & deletion questions

Alice —

Attached are the initial artifacts we discussed: 
- redwood-retention-matrix-2026-03.pdf (policy + configurable fields by deployment type)
- redwood-soc2-evidence-index-2026-03.xlsx (index linking artifacts to control IDs)

Action plan (proposed):
1) We will deliver per-account deletion proof and audit slices for any on-demand deletion requests (deliverable by 2026-04-02).
2) We will provide an EU-region snapshot_gc_report demonstrating in-region deletion of backups for a sample dataset (deliverable by 2026-04-02).
3) If your auditor needs KMS key metadata for Dedicated deployments, we'll request a signed attestation from our Infrastructure team (expected 2026-04-05).

Call: I've booked 30 minutes for Tues 2026-03-30 10:00 AM PT to walk through the evidence index and confirm the final item list. Meeting invite sent separately.

Attachments: redwood-retention-matrix-2026-03.pdf; redwood-soc2-evidence-index-2026-03.xlsx

Regards,
Hannah
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@meditech.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@meditech.com>, ISO Audit Team <iso@meditech.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2/ISO evidence: data residency, retention & deletion questions

Hannah —

Thanks — the matrix and index look useful at first glance. Two additional asks from the ISO reviewer and procurement:

A) ISO mapping: can you include an annex mapping the data lifecycle artifacts to ISO 27001 Annex A controls (particularly A.8.3, A.12.3, A.18.1)? A short one-page mapping is fine.
B) KMS separation: procurement needs confirmation whether Dedicated deployments can use customer-managed KMS keys (or HSM) and whether those keys can be region-bound for EU-only Dedicated instances.

We have an auditor deadline of 2026-04-06 for the full packet. If you can deliver the annex and a KMS attestation/statement by 2026-04-05 that would keep us on schedule.

Attaching a short ISO questionnaire that lists the fields they want populated.

Thanks again — look forward to the per-account demonstrations.

Regards,
Alice Jensen
Sr. IT Compliance Manager
MediTech Solutions
